chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shamūn narrated to me, saying:

I wrote to Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام), asking him to supplicate to Allah for me regarding the pain in my eye. One of my eyes had already gone, and the other was on the verge of going, so he wrote back to me: “May Allah preserve your eye for you.” Then the sound one recovered.

And he wrote at the end of the letter: “May Allah reward you and make your recompense excellent.” I became distressed because of that, and I did not know anyone among my family who had died. Then after some days, news came to me of the death of my son Ṭayyib, and I then knew that the condolence was for him.

key_terms.آجَرَكَ اللَّهُ: may Allah reward you, a phrase used in condolence
key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abū Muḥammad, the kunyah of Imam al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام) in this report
key_terms.ثَوَابَكَ: your reward or recompense from Allah
key_terms.حَبَسَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ عَيْنَكَ: may Allah preserve your eye for you
key_terms.وَجَعِ عَيْنِي: the pain or ailment of my eye
key_terms.يَدْعُوَ اللَّهَ: to supplicate to Allah on someone's behalf

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the effect of the Imam’s du'a and his awareness of an upcoming family death?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) responded to a request for du'a regarding severe eye illness, and the remaining eye recovered by Allah’s leave. The Imam’s written words also contained a condolence formula whose meaning became clear a few days later with the death of the narrator’s son, reflecting both his care and foreknowledge.
